A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix J report original Gridworld and Sepsis simulation results, including counterfactual effect decompositions and state-contribution analyses.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix K retain original simulation results. Appendices L–M add estimation-error and noise-ordering robustness experiments.

M1.justification: The TCFE decomposition, ASE-SV agent attribution, r-SSE-ICC state attribution, and conditional-variance Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The additional validation does not modify these procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Gridworld object delivery with an LLM planner and two RL actors, and the clinician–AI Sepsis simulator. Revised example realizations and additional sampling/order analyses remain within this existing task coverage.

E2.justification: The existing effect and attribution comparisons are retained, with no competing attribution or inference method added or removed. Figure 7 adds ground-truth quantities for estimation validation rather than an alternative decomposition method.

E3.justification: Appendices L–M add direct-computation checks and Sepsis evaluation under five additional random noise orderings; existing sampling budgets and selection thresholds remain unchanged. Figure 2 changes the reported target from total collected reward to discounted total reward, without establishing a rerun. The displayed Gridworld examples also revise Box 1's initial contents.

E4.justification: New Appendix L tests estimation reliability through exact Gridworld calculations and repeated Sepsis evaluations. Appendix M tests sensitivity to noise-monotonicity orderings. These substantially extend validation beyond the retained demonstrations and supplementary analyses in v1.

E5.justification: The five-seed Gridworld error bars are retained. Appendix L.2 adds ten-seed Sepsis repetitions and standard-error distributions for causal effects and attribution scores, including maximum state-score standard errors per action. Figure 6 also clarifies that its existing error bars summarize the 437 selected actions.

E6.justification: Figures 7–9 add exact-reference results, Sepsis variability distributions, and decompositions under five additional orderings, supporting agreement and stability findings. Existing main plots are retained. Displayed Gridworld trajectory totals change from 213.2, 239.0, and 199.0 to 183.2, 199.0, and 209.0, respectively; these are revised example realizations.

T1.justification: The decomposition identity, attribution definitions, noise-monotonicity assumptions, theorems, and appendix proofs are retained. Equation 4's new Unc notation and Appendix N's diagrams express existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: hierarchical counterfactual effect decomposition, Shapley-based agent attribution, intrinsic state contributions, and interpretability demonstrations in two environments.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly proposes partial-identification bounds for non-identifiable settings and notes an efficiency tradeoff. Appendix I.3 explains the inference-cost bottleneck associated with agent capabilities. Appendices L–M add interpretations concerning estimation reliability and sensitivity to the tested orderings.

D1.justification: v2 documents the Gridworld numerical noise ordering and a timing breakdown attributing over 90% of trajectory-sampling time to LLM inference. It references a supplemental README for timing details but removes v1's direct GitHub code URL. Hardware, software, and hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Manski (1990) and Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022) when discussing partial identification, and removes Pearl (2014) and Tsirtsis, De, and Rodriguez (2021). The principal positioning relative to mediation analysis, agent-specific effects, and intrinsic causal contributions remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Local prose tightening, shorter headings, notation clarifications, and expanded appendix navigation refine the presentation. The main section sequence and most existing text remain stable; original Appendices B–J map to C–K after insertion of the notation summary.

P2.justification: v2 reformats the main text and references into two columns, rescales retained displays, and relocates Figure 6 onto a separate page. It adds notation Table 1 and Figures 7–10, covering validation plots, ordering comparisons, and causal diagrams.

improvement.justification: Appendices L–M strengthen confidence in the existing empirical findings through exact Gridworld checks, Sepsis uncertainty reporting, and ordering-sensitivity tests. The notation table and causal diagrams improve clarity. These provide a limited overall improvement in validation and exposition, partly offset by removal of the direct code-access URL.
